# Imagery brief — elevator & escalator

**Written before anything is built**, per FORMATS.md §4.1. Eight images, one block each.

**Where they go.** Save every Gemini export into `markets/elevator/media/` under the
exact `file:` name below. The report builder resolves art from the document's own
folder, that folder's `media/`, and the sibling `../media/` — **not** from the house
`assets/` library — so a report image must live in `markets/elevator/media/` or it will
not render.

**Every prompt below was generated by `scripts/studio/art-prompt.mts`**, which reads the
palette live from `house/tokens.ts`. That is deliberate: a prompt transcribed by hand
drifts, and a colour named in a prompt that is not in the live palette produces art from
a dead visual system. Do not edit the palette, style, frame or background paragraphs —
they are the house brief. The subject line is the only part that is per-image.

**Two laws that bind these.**

- **Illustration is allowed. Photography is real or absent.** Every image here is an
  illustration. Never generate a photograph, and never a generated photograph of a
  person.
- **Compose for the centre.** Every slot is `object-fit: cover`, so the image is scaled
  to fill and the overflow is cropped from the centre. The wide report bands lose their
  top and bottom; the tall carousel panels lose their left and right. Each prompt below
  already says which.

**After the first render, look at it and adjust `imagePos`.** It is a CSS
`object-position` — `50% 30%` keeps the upper-middle, `50% 70%` the lower. One pass of
build → open → adjust → build is the difference between fitting and not.

---

## 1. Report cover hero

```
file:     cover-elevator.jpg
slot:     report cover hero · 5.84 × 2.05 in (2.85:1) · request 16:9
imagePos: 50% 50%
```

**PROMPT**

```
a bank of three closed elevator doors in a building lobby, seen straight on, with call fixtures beside them

PALETTE, STRICT. Flat solid background exactly #FCFAF6 (252, 250, 246) with no gradient,
vignette, texture, border or drop shadow. Bright green #0FA97C for the main masses. Deep
green #0A7A58 for shading. Near-black #16181A for linework. Pure white #FFFFFF only for
highlight surfaces — window glass, a van panel. NO amber, no gold, no brass, no warm
accent of any kind. Use no other colours: no additional greens, no greys, no
off-whites, no blues, no skin tones.

STYLE. Flat editorial vector illustration, isometric 3/4 view, clean geometric
shapes, even weight linework, matte. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not stock-photo.
No lighting, no gradients, no shading within shapes, no ambient occlusion, no cast
shadows, no gloss.

NOTHING IN THE FRAME. No text, no lettering, no numbers, no people, no faces, no
logos, no charts, no graphs.

BACKGROUND. A single uniform fill to all four edges, exactly #FCFAF6. The drawing may
touch the frame; the background behind it must never vary — no vignette, no edge
fade, no gradient background, no drop shadow, no border, no frame, no darkening at
the corners.

COMPOSITION. Landscape, 1700 × 596. The image is cropped from the centre to fill its slot, so keep the subject centred with generous empty background at the TOP and BOTTOM; nothing important within 8% of any edge.
```

## What to do when they come back

1. Save each into `markets/elevator/media/` under its `file:` name.
2. **Check the corners before anything is built:**
   `npx tsx $REPO/scripts/studio/art-prompt.mts --check markets/elevator/media`
   It samples all four corners of every image and reports on-palette, drifted warm,
   drifted dark, or non-uniform. The brief demands a uniform flat background to all four
   edges, so the corners are exactly where drift shows.
3. Then `design-check.mts` on each spec, which verifies every requested image actually
   resolves and that its aspect ratio survives a centre crop.
4. Then build, then **look at both bookends** — not just the dark one.

## One note on the house library

`assets/trades/elevator.png` already exists and reads on-palette at exactly
(252, 250, 246). It is square at 2048 × 2048, so in a 476 × 1102 carousel panel it would
lose more than half its width. It is fine as a fallback and wrong as a first choice,
which is why images 6 and 7 are specified fresh.
